q: tell me about the Voynich manuscript
a: The Voynich Manuscript is widely considered the most mysterious unsolved manuscript in the world. Discovered by antique book dealer Wilfrid Voynich in 1912, the manuscript is a 240-page codex written in an entirely unknown script and language that has defied all attempts at decryption for over a century. It is carbon-dated to the early 15th century (1404-1438 CE). The manuscript is illustrated with intricate drawings of unknown plants that don't match any known species, astronomical diagrams with symbols no one can identify, biological illustrations of naked women in strange green liquid, and what appear to be pharmaceutical recipes. Numerous cryptographers, linguists, and AI systems have attempted to decode it. Some theories suggest it is a cipher for a known language, a constructed language, a hoax, or glossolalia (speaking in tongues). In 2019, a researcher claimed it was written in a proto-Romance language, but this remains controversial and unverified. The manuscript is currently held at the Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library at Yale University. Other mysterious manuscripts include the Codex Seraphinianus (a modern illustrated encyclopedia of an imaginary world), the Rohonc Codex, and the Liber Linteus.
